> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf76922925917c9841d69b4a5eda77762fc136cf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9b9135e8221898dee66527c1c4d5e168840fe633` — the merge of head `2ff4b92cb69e58a4d0bd6fa15c76e89bb10ca437` into base `bf76922925917c9841d69b4a5eda77762fc136cf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9b9135e8221898dee66527c1c4d5e168840fe633 && git checkout 9b9135e8221898dee66527c1c4d5e168840fe633
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bf76922925917c9841d69b4a5eda77762fc136cf 2ff4b92cb69e58a4d0bd6fa15c76e89bb10ca437 && git checkout -B drift-repro bf76922925917c9841d69b4a5eda77762fc136cf && git merge --no-ff 2ff4b92cb69e58a4d0bd6fa15c76e89bb10ca437

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf76922925917c9841d69b4a5eda77762fc136cf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bf76922925917c9841d69b4a5eda77762fc136cf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3690b8ef570cce5285675607e29e346b77cb9a73`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json + packages/client/src/index.ts, content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx, content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx, .changeset/34189-pending-action-decide-session.md
Security-touching: yes

Read at 2026-11-16T02:14Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6905370348; lane request 6905360702 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

No prior record on this PR; findings are numbered fresh and continue no earlier id.

### ① Derived judgments

Read against the contract PR #34001 landed (`fa1fb6f4e`): `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, section "The in-app assistant door: the same rule, its own channel", the docblocks of `IAIService.proposePendingAction` / `approvePendingAction` / `rejectPendingAction`, and the semantic entry `18.in-app-pending-action-decided-by-person.ts`. The diff was read as the head against its merged main parent `b51cb18a7`: 6 files, +53/−9.

- **Who decides.** "Only the person the call ran as approves or rejects the item" (skill, both docs pages, three docblocks) is point 1 of the contract, word for word in substance. "Another user's `ai:approve` does not decide it" is the same point. Holds.
- **Which credential.** "On their signed-in session to the app; an API key or token is refused, even the person's own" is point 2 together with rule 4's last sentence. Holds as far as it goes; it leaves out one refused class the contract names (S2).
- **As whom it runs.** `actions-as-tools.mdx` drops "approve re-runs the same dispatcher" for "approve runs the action as that person with every gate re-checked". That is point 3, and the dropped phrase is the contract's FROM reading. Holds.
- **Second approver.** "A second approver goes through the approvals engine (the `held` outcome)" is point 1's last sentence and the `approvePendingAction` docblock. Holds; its placement in the skill creates a misreading (S1).
- **Listing.** "A client on a token can still list and get" keeps the existing `ai:read` text; the contract puts none of the deciding points on `listPendingActions`. Holds.
- **Refusal code.** No code is quoted for the new refusals. Correct: the contract registers an envelope for the MCP doors only and names none for the in-app decide doors, and no package in this repository serves the decide routes (`git grep pending-actions` over `packages/**` finds the client and the protocol schemas only). The existing "handle the 403" for the `ai:read` / `ai:approve` split is unchanged.
- **Docblock-only.** Every changed line of `packages/client/src/index.ts` is a comment line; no signature, export, route string or statement moved.
- **Eval.** Case 6 matches the file's schema (`id`, `prompt`, `expected_output`, `files`, `assertions.must_contain` / `must_not_contain`, as cases 1 to 5). Its expected output contains all three `must_contain` strings and neither `must_not_contain` string. The prompt asks for the forbidden act on a token, and the expected answer declines it and lists instead, so it tests the taught rule.
- **Other skills and pages.** `git grep` over `skills/**` for pending action, `ai:approve`, `pending_approval`, `enableActionApproval`: only `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` teaches the queue, and its other two mentions (the skip rule, pitfall 1) say nothing about who decides. Over `content/docs` outside the release-owned and generated trees, only the two pages in this diff teach deciding. No fifth site is left. No link was added or changed.
- **Not derivable here.** The decide doors live in the cloud repository and cloud#4607 is not readable from this seat. Whatever goes beyond the contract text is therefore unconfirmed, which is S3.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` patch and `@objectstack/client` patch: right. Skill wording and docblock text only; the client docblock ships in its declaration file, so the client entry is owed. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right on the PR body and the changeset: nothing an author wrote parses differently, and the narrowing itself was declared by #34001. No package is missing: the two docs pages publish with no package.

CI on this head: 72 check-runs, all completed; 60 success, 12 skipped (opt-in and path-gated jobs), none failed, none running.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H.** `skills/**` is on the governed register and the low-risk arm does not apply (`Security-touching: yes`, a client package release in the same PR). This lands on the maintainer's word only. The PR is a draft, correctly.
- **Security-touching: yes.** The changed hunks teach credential, token and permission behaviour: who may decide a pending action and on which credential. This record stays at the rule layer.
- **Landing order (card item 4).** The contract's "When it binds" section says the in-app door runs the earlier queue until its implementing change ships. Every sentence this PR adds is the TO reading, stated without condition. It is true of the contract on main and becomes true of the door only with the cloud release that carries cloud#4607. The maintainer merges in that release window or after it, not before. This seat cannot confirm the state of cloud#4607.
- **Dev open question (name the refusal code later?).** Answer A, leave "refused" with no code. Main states none for these doors.
- **Dev out-of-scope finding (`actions-as-tools.mdx`).** Taken into this PR by the seat's surface widening 6905036822; reviewed above.
- **Tier of authorship.** Authored below the mandated tier under the maintainer's quota ruling, declared in the PR body; this record is the at-tier review that ruling routes to a review seat.
- SQL push-down: no query, join or id materialisation in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

S1 (should-fix) — `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, Human-in-the-loop paragraph: the new clause ends "(the `held` outcome)." and the unchanged next sentence begins "Whether *your* action is held is decided entirely by the skip rule above". Before this change "held" there could only mean "queued for approval". Now it follows the named `held` outcome and reads as that outcome, which is false: `held` is a host policy's decision after the person approved, and `actionSkipReason` / `actionRequiresApproval` say nothing about it. Reword the old sentence ("Whether *your* action is queued …") or move the second-approver clause after it.

S2 (should-fix) — the skill, both docs pages and the docblocks name "an API key or token" as refused and stop there. The contract's point 2, the `IAIService` docblocks and the migration entry all name one more refused class in the same breath: an AI identity, and any call that arrives through an AI door; rule 5 adds that the model's own confirmation never counts. A skill is read by an agent, and that clause is the one addressed to its reader. Add it at least to the skill ("…an API key, a token or an AI identity is refused…; the assistant never decides its own item"), and to eval 6's expected output if the wording allows. The headroom covers it (6019 of 6801).

S3 (should-fix) — `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`: "Deciding (approve or reject) takes `ai:approve` AND the person's own signed-in session". The contract on main says another user's `ai:approve` does not decide; it does not say the person needs `ai:approve` to decide their own item, and the enforcing door is not in this repository. The sentence asserts a precondition no source on main carries. The card's item 2 asked for this wording, so it is not held against the dev. Before landing, the seat confirms with the cloud lane whether the person's own decision still takes `ai:approve`, and otherwise words it as the skill does ("another user's `ai:approve` does not decide it").

N1 (nit) — `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`, two lines below the changed sentence: "operators expect single-click yes/no". The decider is now the person, not an operator. This answers the seat's hand-off question: change the word.

N2 (nit) — `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`, the unchanged closing comment of the same block: "These methods are for everything that is not a component — server code, jobs, CLIs, tests." For approve and reject that no longer holds, by the comment this PR adds a few lines above. One qualifying clause would do.

N3 (nit) — eval 6 assertions: `must_contain` "list" matches almost any answer, and `must_not_contain` "/approve" fails a correct answer that names the refused route to explain why it is refused. "pendingActions.list" and dropping "/approve" (the method-call string already discriminates) would be tighter.

N4 (nit) — the changeset says the four places "now say what the confirmation rule says" and states the refusals without condition. One clause that the door enforces this from the runtime release that carries the in-app door, not from this package release, would keep a changelog reader from taking it as that release note; the migration entry tells them to look for exactly that note.

Against the card's scenario (an operator script on a token told to approve the queue): the skill, as written, turns that request down and points at listing and at `held`. Nothing it teaches gives an agent, a script or a stored credential a way to decide for the person. It holds against the contract it teaches, with S1 to S3 as the gaps.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f407440dd96a697faa6cbb3a7e9f861ba28fbea0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json + packages/client/src/index.ts, content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx, content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx, .changeset/34189-pending-action-decide-session.md
Security-touching: yes

Read at 2026-11-16T02:46Z. Delta review of this head against PASS 6905434558 at 3690b8ef; claim: comment 6905842681; lane request 6905824119 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Delta read: one fix commit `ef01e36b9` (6 files, +26/−23) and the merge commit `f407440dd` of main (merge base now `7be32d39`). `git diff ef01e36b9 f407440dd` over the six paths is empty, so the merge brought nothing into them; the PR's whole diff against the new base is the same six files, +58/−11. Findings below are numbered fresh; each says which prior id it continues.

### ① Derived judgments

Read against `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts` at this head: rule 4's closing paragraph, rule 5, the section "The in-app assistant door: the same rule, its own channel" (points 1 to 3 and its closing paragraph) and "When it binds".

Prior findings, by id:

- **S1 (prior), closed.** The skill's sentence now reads "Whether *your* action is queued is decided entirely by the skip rule above". "held" appears once in the paragraph, as the named outcome. The second-approver clause stayed in place, which the prior record offered as one of two fixes.
- **S2 (prior), closed on the refused class; changed on rule 5.** The skill now says "an API key or token (even the person's own) is refused, and so is an AI identity and any call that arrives through an AI door". That is point 2 and rule 4, no more. The three client docblocks, `client-sdk.mdx` and `actions-as-tools.mdx` add "an AI identity" in their existing clause; the contract's own parenthesis defines an AI identity as including a call through an AI door, so the shorter form is not a narrowing. Eval 6's expected output names both. The rule 5 sentence is the contract's closing sentence of the in-app section word for word, but the skill carries it without the scope the contract gives it. That is S1 below.
- **S3 (prior), closed.** `client-sdk.mdx` no longer says deciding takes `ai:approve`; it now says "Another user's `ai:approve` does not decide it", the skill's wording. `git grep` at this head over `skills`, `content/docs`, `packages/client` and `.changeset` for the old precondition and for "whatever they hold" finds nothing. The class docblock's older paragraph (reads and decisions separately permissioned, handle the 403) is unchanged text from main and states no precondition for the person's own decision. The changeset never carried one.
- **N1 (prior), closed.** "people expect single-click yes/no".
- **N2 (prior), closed.** The closing comment adds "(approve and reject excepted: those are the person's own act in the app)".
- **N3 (prior), closed.** `must_contain` is "pendingActions.list", "signed-in session", "refused"; `must_not_contain` is the method-call string alone. The file parses; case 6's expected output holds all three required strings and not the forbidden one. The prompt names `@objectstack/client`, so requiring the client's list call is tight without being brittle.
- **N4 (prior), closed.** The changeset adds "The door enforces this from the runtime release that carries the in-app door, not from this package release", which is "When it binds" in one clause.

Other judgments on the delta:

- **Docblock-only, still.** Every changed line of `packages/client/src/index.ts` in `ef01e36b9` is a comment line.
- **Skill budgets.** 434 lines, 24235 bytes. The PR body reports 6054 tokens against the 6801 ceiling (headroom 747); the token ratchet runs in CI and CI is green on this head.
- **Not derivable here.** Unchanged from the prior record: the decide doors are not in this repository, so nothing beyond the contract text is confirmed by this seat.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: `@objectstack/skills` patch, `@objectstack/client` patch, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The fix commit changes prose, docblock text and eval strings only.

CI on this head (`f407440dd`): 72 check-runs, all completed; 60 success, 12 skipped, none failed, none running. The PR is open, a draft, mergeable state clean.

CI completed before posting: 72 check-runs on this head, 60 success, 12 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H.** Unchanged. `skills/**` is governed and `Security-touching: yes`; this lands on the maintainer's word only. The PR stays a draft, correctly.
- **Security-touching: yes.** The changed hunks teach who may decide a pending action and on which credential. This record stays at the rule layer.
- **Landing order.** Unchanged: every sentence is the TO reading. The maintainer merges with or after the runtime release that carries the in-app door, not before. The changeset now says so itself. This seat cannot confirm the state of that release.
- **PR body.** Its first verification line still expects "6019 / 6801"; the figure after round 1 is 6054, as the same body says further down. The body is not the diff; the dev corrects the line.
- SQL push-down: no query, join or id materialisation in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

S1 (should-fix) — continues prior S2 (introduced by its fix). `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, Human-in-the-loop paragraph: "Neither the model's own confirmation nor the caller's `confirm` counts." In the contract that sentence closes the in-app section and goes on "(rule 5): the item waits for the person"; rule 5 itself is scoped to a declared-gated action call. The skill drops both scopes, and has not introduced `confirm` at that point. Some forty lines below, the same skill's MCP table tells the reader to send `confirm: true` on `delete_record` and `delete_records` after asking the human, and on `run_action` for an action flagged `ai.requiresConfirmation`. Read together, the file now says `confirm` does not count and tells the reader to send it. The data-tool rows are not what rule 5 speaks of, and the `run_action` row is the prescription "When it binds" leaves to the change that enforces the MCP door, so those rows are not this PR's to move. Scope the new sentence to the queue instead, for example: "The model's own confirmation does not decide the item, and neither does a `confirm` on the call: the item waits for the person." Eval 6 already words it within scope and needs no change.

N1 (nit) — new. `packages/client/src/index.ts` class docblock and `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`: "…is refused, and so is an AI identity: such a client can list and get, never decide." After the inserted clause, "such a client" reads as covering the AI identity too. The contract puts no deciding point on listing and says nothing either way about what an AI identity may list. Put the AI identity clause after the "lists, does not decide" clause, or end the sentence before it.

N2 (nit) — continues prior N3, not a regression. `must_not_contain` "pendingActions.approve(" still fails a correct answer that quotes the call in order to say it is refused. The prior record accepted this string; it is noted so the eval's owner knows the edge, not asked of this round.
